(1962–1965) | pushpin_map = Spain | coordinates1 = {{coord|41.380833|2.122778|display=inline}} | pushpin_mark1 = Red pog.svg | pushpin_label1 = '''Barcelona''' | pushpin_label1_position = left | coordinates2 = {{coord|40.453056|-3.688361|display=inline}} | pushpin_mark2 = Blue pog.svg | pushpin_label2 = '''Real Madrid''' | pushpin_label2_position = right }} '''El Clásico''' (in Spanish, also in [[lowercase letters]];{{cite web |title=el clásico, en minúscula y sin comillas |url=https://www.fundeu.es/recomendacion/el-clasico-en-minuscula-y-sin-comillas/ |website=fundeu.es |access-date=2 March 2020 |language=es}} {{IPA|es|el ˈklasiko}}) or '''El Clàssic''' (in [[Catalan language|Catalan]],{{cite web |url=http://www.elpunt.cat/noticia/article/8-esports/48-barca/329919-el-classic-es-jugara-dilluns.html |publisher=[[El Punt]] |access-date=18 November 2010 |date=18 November 2010 |title=El clàssic es jugarà dilluns |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101231000103/http://www.elpunt.cat/noticia/article/8-esports/48-barca/329919-el-classic-es-jugara-dilluns.html |archive-date=31 December 2010}} {{IPA|ca|əl ˈklasik|pron}}), both meaning "The Classic", is the name given to any [[Association football|football]] match between rival clubs [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]. Originally referring to competitions held in the [[La Liga|Spanish championship]], the term now includes every match between the clubs, such as those in the [[UEFA Champions League]], [[Copa del Rey]], and [[Supercopa de España]]. It is considered one of sport's fiercest rivalries, and its matches have a global audience of hundreds of millions.{{cite news |last=Stevenson |first=Jonathan |title=Barca & Real renew El Clasico rivalry |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/7773758.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=12 December 2008 |access-date=15 August 2010}}[https://www.forbes.com/sites/kurtbadenhausen/2014/05/16/lionel-messi-agrees-to-new-50-million-a-year-deal-with-barcelona/ "Lionel Messi Reaches $50 Million-A-Year Deal With Barcelona"]. Forbes. Retrieved 1 October 2014{{cite news |last=Rookwood |first=Dan |title=The bitterest rivalry in world football |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/aug/28/sport.danrookwood |work=[[The Guardian]] |location=London |date=28 August 2002}}[https://web.archive.org/web/20140816175537/http://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/clubs/rivalries/newsid=106848/ "El Clasico: When stars collide"]. FIFA.com. Retrieved 21 October 2014 A fixture known for its intensity, it has featured memorable [[goal celebration]]s from both teams, often involving mockery from both sides. The fixture is politicised due to the [[Catalan independence movement]], as [[Madrid]] is the capital and largest city in Spain and [[Barcelona]] is the capital and largest city of the autonomous community of [[Catalonia]]; the two teams are hence respectively [[Party identification|identified]] with [[Spanish nationalism|Spanish unionism]] and [[Catalan nationalism|Catalan separatism]].{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2017/oct/02/barcelona-in-strange-and-symbolic-eye-of-a-storm-over-catalonia |title=Barcelona in the strange and symbolic eye of a storm over Catalonia |newspaper=The Guardian |date=2 October 2017 |access-date=9 January 2018}} They are [[List of football clubs by competitive honours won|among the wealthiest and most successful football clubs in the world]]; in 2024, ''[[Forbes]]'' ranked Real Madrid and Barcelona among the most valuable football teams in the world, in first and third place respectively.{{cite web |last1=Ozanian |first1=Mike |last2=Teitelbaum |first2=Justin |title=World's Most Valuable Soccer Teams|url=https://www.forbes.com/lists/soccer-valuations/ |website=Forbes |access-date=20 May 2025 |date=23 May 2024}} As of the match played on 10 May 2026, the teams are tied in head-to-head results in official competitive matches with 106 wins each, along with 52 draws.{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/el-clasico |title=Barça and Real Madrid: El Clásico |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=26 October 2025}}{{cite news |url=https://cadenaser.com/nacional/2023/03/02/las-estadisticas-del-clasico-partidos-goles-y-datos-de-los-enfrentamientos-entre-real-madrid-y-barcelona-cadena-ser/?outputType=amp |title=Las estadísticas del Clásico: partidos, goles y datos de los enfrentamientos entre Real Madrid y Barcelona |newspaper=Cadena Ser |date=4 April 2023 |access-date=23 May 2023 |language=es}}{{cite news |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/el-clasico-barca-real-madrid/20170728/43102933574/barca-madrid-clasico-amistoso.html?facet=amp |title=26 años sin un Clásico amistoso |newspaper=Mundo Deportivo |date=28 July 2017 |access-date=23 May 2023 |language=es}}{{cite news |url=https://www.lagalerna.com/los-amistosos-real-madrid-barcelona/ |title=Los amistosos Real Madrid–Barcelona |newspaper=La Galerna |date=29 July 2017 |access-date=23 May 2023 |language=es}} Along with [[Athletic Bilbao]], they are the only clubs in [[La Liga]] never to have been relegated. {{TOC limit|3}} == Rivalry == === History === [[File:Real Madrid - Barça (3495454182).jpg|thumb|[[Bernabéu Stadium|Bernabéu]] (before renovation), the home of Real Madrid, before El Clásico]] [[File:Camp nou before F.C. Barcelona - Real Madrid league match of 2012.JPG|thumb|[[Camp Nou]] (before renovation), the home of FC Barcelona, before El Clásico. The fans of Barcelona are creating a mosaic of the [[Senyera|Catalan flag]].]] The conflict between Real Madrid and Barcelona has long surpassed the sporting dimension,Palomares, Cristina [https://books.google.com/books?id=UM_DyqqVUlIC&PA=231 ''The quest for survival after Franco: moderate Francoism and the slow journey''], p.231''[[Cambio 16]]'', 6–12, Enero 1975 p.18 so much that elections to the clubs' presidencies have been strongly politicized. [[Phil Ball (writer)|Phil Ball]], the author of ''Morbo: The Story of Spanish Football'', says about the match, "they hate each other with an intensity that can truly shock the outsider".{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/apr/21/championsleague.sport |work=The Guardian |location=London |title=Mucho morbo |date=21 April 2002 |access-date=1 May 2010 |first=Phil |last=Ball}} As early as the 1930s, Barcelona "had developed a reputation as a symbol of Catalan identity, opposed to the centralising tendencies of Madrid".Ham, Anthony p. 221 In 1936, when [[Francisco Franco]] started the ''[[Spanish coup of July 1936|coup d'état]]'' against the democratic [[Second Spanish Republic]], the president of Barcelona, [[Josep Sunyol]], member of the [[Republican Left of Catalonia]] and Deputy to [[Cortes Generales|The Cortes]], was arrested and executed without trial by Franco's troopsMcNeill, Donald (1999) [https://books.google.com/books?id=zfiyEutRtmQC&pg=PA61 ''Urban change and the European left: tales from the new Barcelona''] p.61 (Sunyol was exercising his political activities, visiting Republican troops north of Madrid).Burns, Jimmy, 'Don Patricio O'Connell: An Irishman and the Politics of Spanish Football' in "{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20081121050623/http://www.irishargentine.org/0803.pdf Irish Migration Studies in Latin America]}}" 6:1 (March 2008), p. 44. Available online [https://www.irlandeses.org/0803burns3.htm pg. 3], [https://www.irlandeses.org/0803burns4.htm pg. 4]. Retrieved 29 August 2010. During the dictatorships of [[Miguel Primo de Rivera]] and especially [[Francoist Spain|Francisco Franco]], all regional languages and identities in Spain were frowned upon and restrained. As such, most citizens of Barcelona were in strong opposition to the fascist-like regime.{{cite web |url=https://www.barcelona.cat/museuhistoria/sites/default/files/seat.pdf |title=Barcelona malgrat el franquisme |publisher=[[Museum of the History of Barcelona|MUHBA]] |date=December 2012 |access-date=18 February 2024 |language=ca}} In this period, Barcelona gained their motto ''Més que un club'' (''English: More than a club'') because of its alleged connection to [[Catalan nationalism|Catalan nationalist]] as well as to [[progressivism|progressive]] beliefs.Ball, Phil p. 88 There is an ongoing controversy as to what extent Franco's rule (1939–75) influenced the activities and on-pitch results of both Barcelona and Real Madrid. Most historians agree that Franco did not have a preferred football team, but his Spanish nationalist beliefs led him to associate himself with the establishment teams, such as [[Atlético Madrid|Atlético Aviación]] and [[Real Madrid CF|Madrid FC]] (which recovered its ''royal'' name after the fall of the Republic). On the other hand, he also wanted the renamed ''CF Barcelona'' to succeed as a "Spanish team" rather than a Catalan one.{{cite web |url=https://thesefootballtimes.co/2017/09/27/real-madrid-and-the-franco-regime/ |title=The story of Real Madrid and the Franco regime |first=Nick |last=Fitzgerald |website=thesefootballtimes.co |date=27 September 2017 |access-date=1 July 2022}}{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/general-franco-real-madrid-king-history-behind-clubs-link/fcoqldp8h2bb1841o2rspmuhe |title=General Franco, Real Madrid & the king: The history behind club's link to Spain's establishment |first=Ryan |last=Kelly |website=goal.com |access-date=1 July 2022}} During the early years of Franco's rule, Real Madrid were not particularly successful, winning two [[Copa del Rey|Copa del Generalísimo]] titles and a [[Copa Eva Duarte]]; Barcelona claimed three [[List of Spanish football champions|league titles]], one Copa del Generalísimo and one Copa Eva Duarte. During that period, Atlético Aviación were believed to be the preferred team over Real Madrid. Events of the period include Real Madrid's [[Real Madrid v FC Barcelona (1943 Copa del Generalísimo)|11–1]] home win against Barcelona in the [[1943 Copa del Generalísimo|Copa del Generalísimo]], where the Catalan team alleged intimidation, and the controversial transfer of [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]] to Real Madrid despite his agreement with Barcelona. The latter transfer was part of Real Madrid chairman [[Santiago Bernabéu (footballer)|Santiago Bernabéu]]'s "revolution" that ushered in the era of unprecedented dominance. Bernabéu, himself a veteran of the Civil War who fought for [[Nationalist faction (Spanish Civil War)|Franco's forces]], saw Real Madrid on top not only of Spanish but also European football, helping create the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]], the first true competition for Europe's best club sides. His vision was fulfilled when Real Madrid not only started winning consecutive league titles but also won the first five editions of the European Cup in the 1950s.{{cite web |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/about-real-madrid/history/presidents/santiago-bernabeu |title=SANTIAGO BERNABÉU 1943–1978 |publisher=Real Madrid C.F. |website=realmadrid.com |access-date=1 July 2022}} These events had a profound impact on Spanish football and influenced Franco's attitude. According to historians, during this time he realized the importance of Real Madrid for his regime's international image, and the club became his preferred team until his death.{{cite web |title=¿Tenía un trato preferente el Real Madrid en el franquismo? |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/deportes/20230418/8905180/tenia-trato-preferente-real-madrid-franquismo.html |date=18 April 2023 |access-date=21 July 2023 |publisher=[[La Vanguardia]] |language=es}} [[Fernando Maria Castiella]], who served as [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Spain)|Minister of Foreign Affairs]] under Franco from 1957 until 1969, noted that "[Real Madrid] is the best embassy we have ever had." Franco died in 1975, and the [[Spanish transition to democracy]] soon followed. Under his rule, [[List of Real Madrid CF records and statistics#Honours|Real Madrid had won]] 14 league titles, 6 Copa del Generalísimo titles, 1 Copa Eva Duarte, 6 European Cups, 2 [[Latin Cup]]s and 1 [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]]. In the same period, [[List of FC Barcelona records and statistics#Honours|Barcelona had won]] 8 league titles, 9 Copa del Generalísimo titles, 3 Copa Eva Duarte titles, 3 [[Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]]s, and 2 Latin Cups. The image for both clubs was further affected by the creation of [[ultras]] groups, some of which became [[Football hooliganism|hooligans]]. In 1980, Ultras Sur was founded as a far-right-leaning Real Madrid ultras group, followed in 1981 by the foundation of the – initially left-leaning, and later on far-right – Barcelona ultras group [[Boixos Nois]]. Both groups became known for their violent acts,{{cite web |url=https://elcentrocampista.com/2011/10/eternal-shame-real-madrid-and-the-ultra-sur/ |title=The Ultra Sur | El Centrocampista - Spanish Football and La Liga News in English |publisher=El Centrocampista |date=27 October 2011 |access-date=20 October 2013}}{{cite web |author=Dos Manzanas |url=http://www.dosmanzanas.com/2011/06/tres-boixos-nois-detenidos-por-agredir-a-una-mujer-transexual-en-barcelona.html |title=Tres Boixos Nois detenidos por agredir a una mujer transexual en Barcelona |publisher=Dos manzanas |date=14 June 2011 |access-date=20 October 2013}} and one of the most conflictive factions of Barcelona supporters, the ''Casuals'', became a full-fledged criminal organisation.{{cite web |url=https://www.elperiodico.com/es/noticias/sociedad/20100911/mafia-boixos-nois-especializo-atracar-narcos/474828.shtml |title=La mafia de boixos nois se especializó en atracar a narcos – Sociedad |date=11 September 2010 |website=Elperiodico.com |access-date=20 October 2013}} For many people, Barcelona is still considered "the [[rebellious]] club", or the alternative pole to "Real Madrid's [[conservatism]]".{{cite web |url=http://www.vavel.com/en/football/scottish-premier-league/celtic-glasgow/148824-the-green-guardiola.html |title=Great similarities between Barcelona and Celtic |website=vavel.com |date=21 April 2012 |access-date=5 December 2012}}{{cite web |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/fourfourtwos-50-biggest-derbies-world-no2-barcelona-vs-real-madrid#:JmuVBbQMXViUeA |title=FourFourTwo's 50 Biggest Derbies in the World, No.2: Barcelona vs Real Madrid |website=fourfourtwo.com |date=29 April 2016 |access-date=30 May 2016}} According to polls released by CIS (Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas), Real Madrid is the favorite team of the most Spanish residents, while Barcelona stands in second position. In Catalonia, forces of all the political spectrum are overwhelmingly in favour of Barcelona. Nevertheless, the support of the blaugrana club (Barcelona) goes far beyond from that region, earning its best results among young people, sustainers of a federal structure of Spain and citizens with [[left-wing]] ideology, in contrast with Real Madrid fans which politically tend to adopt [[right-wing]] views.{{cite web |url=http://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/noticias/20090720/53749146392/la-izquierda-es-cule-y-la-derecha-merengue-segun-el-cis-madrid-fc-barcelona-barsa-real-madrid-espany.html |title=La izquierda es culé y la derecha, merengue, según el CIS |website=LaVanguardia.com |language=es |date=20 July 2009 |access-date=4 September 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200227045737/https://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20090720/53749146392/la-izquierda-es-cule-y-la-derecha-merengue-segun-el-cis.html |archive-date=27 February 2020 |url-status=dead}}{{cite news |url=https://elpais.com/diario/2003/02/28/deportes/1046386805_850215.html |title=¿Del Madrid o del Barça? |work=El País |language=es |date=23 February 2003 |access-date=21 November 2015 |last1=Rusiñol |first1=Pere}} ===1943 Copa del Generalísimo semi-finals=== {{Main|Real Madrid v FC Barcelona (1943 Copa del Generalísimo)}} [[file:Marca portada rmadrid 11 vs 1 barcelona.jpg|thumb|Cover of ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' newspaper titled "an extraordinary match of Real Madrid" to describe the 11–1 win over Barcelona]] On 13 June 1943, Real Madrid beat Barcelona 11–1 at the [[Estadio Chamartín|Chamartín]] in the second leg of the [[Copa del Rey|Copa del Generalísimo]] semi-finals (the Copa del Presidente de la República{{cite web |url=https://www.fmf.com.mx/mobil/copa_del_presidente_de_la_ii_republica_1932__1936.htm |title=Copa del Presidente de la II República 1932 – 1936}} having been renamed in honour of [[General Franco]]).{{cite news |title=Real Madrid v Barcelona: six of the best 'El Clásicos' |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/la-liga/8946213/Real-Madrid-v-Barcelona-six-of-the-best-El-Clasicos.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/la-liga/8946213/Real-Madrid-v-Barcelona-six-of-the-best-El-Clasicos.html |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |newspaper=The Telegraph |access-date=19 December 2011 |date=9 December 2011 |location=London}}{{cbignore}} The first leg, played at the [[Camp de Les Corts|Les Corts]] in Catalonia, had ended with Barcelona winning 3–0. Madrid complained about all the three goals that referee Fombona Fernández had allowed for Barcelona, with the home supporters also whistling Madrid throughout, whom they accused of employing roughhouse tactics, and Fombona for allowing them to. Barça's [[Josep Escolà]] was stretchered off in the first half with José María Querejeta's stud marks in his stomach. A campaign began in Madrid. The newspaper ''[[Ya (newspaper)|Ya]]'' reported the whistling as a "clear intention to attack the representatives of Spain."{{cite book |page=25 |author=[[Phil Ball (writer)|Phil Ball]] |title=Morbo: the story of Spanish football |publisher=WSC Books |location=Reading |year=2001}} Barcelona player Josep Valle recalled: "The press officer at the DND and ABC newspaper wrote all sorts of scurrilous lies, really terrible things, winding up the Madrid fans like never before". Former Real Madrid goalkeeper [[Eduardo Teus]], who admitted that Madrid had "above all played hard", wrote in a newspaper: "the ground itself made Madrid concede two of the three goals, goals that were totally unfair"."[https://books.google.com/books?id=2l6zHv_reuUC&pg=PA68 Sid Lowe: Fear and loathing in La Liga.. Barcelona vs Real Madrid]" p. 68. Random House. 26 September 2013 Barcelona fans were banned from traveling to Madrid. Real Madrid released a statement after the match which former club president [[Ramón Mendoza]] explained, "The message got through that those fans who wanted to could go to El Club bar on Calle de la Victoria where Madrid's social center was. There, they were given a whistle. Others had whistles handed to them with their tickets." The day of the second leg, the Barcelona team were insulted and stones were thrown at their bus as soon as they left their hotel. Barcelona's striker [[Mariano Gonzalvo]] said of the incident, "Five minutes before the game had started, our penalty area was already full of coins." Barcelona goalkeeper [[Lluis Miró]] rarely approached his line—when he did, he was armed with stones. As [[Francisco Calvet]] told the story, "They were shouting: ''Reds! Separatists!''... a bottle just missed Sospedra that would have killed him if it had hit him. It was all set up.""[https://books.google.com/books?id=2l6zHv_reuUC&pg=PA70 Sid Lowe: Fear and loathing in La Liga.. Barcelona vs Real Madrid]" p. 70. Random House. 26 September 2013 Real Madrid went 2–0 up within half an hour. The third goal brought with it a sending off for Barcelona's Benito García after he made what Calvet claimed was a "completely normal tackle". Madrid's [[José Llopis Corona]] recalled, "At which point, they got a bit demoralized," while Ángel Mur countered, "at which point, we thought: 'go on then, score as many as you want'." Madrid scored in minutes 31', 33', 35', 39', 43' and 44', as well as two goals ruled out for offside, made it 8–0. [[Juan Antonio Samaranch|Juan Samaranch]] wrote: "In that atmosphere and with a referee who wanted to avoid any complications, it was humanly impossible to play... If the azulgranas had played badly, really badly, the scoreboard would still not have reached that astronomical figure. The point is that they did not play at all."Lowe, Sid. p. 74 Both clubs were fined 2,500 pesetas by the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] and, although Barcelona appealed, it made no difference. Piñeyro resigned in protest, complaining of "a campaign that the press has run against Barcelona for a week and which culminated in the shameful day at Chamartín".{{cite book |last=Spaaij |first=Ramn |title=Understanding football hooliganism: a comparison of six Western European football clubs |year=2006 |publisher=Amsterdam University Press |location=Amsterdam |isbn=978-90-5629-445-8 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=i21W_KN_iUMC&pg=284 |access-date=19 December 2011}}Lowe, Sid. p. 73 The match report in the newspaper ''La Prensa'' described Barcelona's only goal as a "reminder that there was a team there who knew how to play football and that if they did not do so that afternoon, it was not exactly their fault".Lowe, Sid. p. 72 Another newspaper called the scoreline "as absurd as it was abnormal". According to football writer [[Sid Lowe]], "There have been relatively few mentions of the game [since] and it is not a result that has been particularly celebrated in Madrid. Indeed, the 11–1 occupies a far more prominent place in Barcelona's history. This was the game that first formed the identification of Madrid as the team of the dictatorship and Barcelona as its victims.""[https://books.google.com/books?id=2l6zHv_reuUC&pg=PA67 Sid Lowe: Fear and loathing in La Liga.. Barcelona vs Real Madrid]" p. 67. Random House. 26 September 2013 Fernando Argila, Barcelona's reserve goalkeeper from the game, said, "There was no rivalry. Not, at least, until that game.""[https://books.google.com/books?id=2l6zHv_reuUC&pg=PA77 Sid Lowe: Fear and loathing in La Liga.. Barcelona vs Real Madrid]" p. 77. Random House. 26 September 2013 ===Di Stéfano transfer=== [[File:Di stefano real madrid cf (cropped).png|thumb|upright|[[Alfredo Di Stéfano]]'s controversial 1953 transfer to Real Madrid instead of Barcelona intensified the rivalry.]] The rivalry was intensified during the 1950s when the clubs disputed the signing of Argentine forward Alfredo Di Stéfano. Di Stéfano had impressed both Barcelona and Real Madrid while playing for [[Club Deportivo Los Millonarios|Los Millonarios]] in [[Bogotá]], Colombia, during a players' strike in his native Argentina. Soon after Millonarios' return to Colombia, Barcelona directors visited Buenos Aires and agreed with River Plate, the last FIFA-affiliated team to have held Di Stéfano's rights, for his transfer in 1954 for the equivalent of 150 million Italian lira ($200,000 according to other sources{{specify|date=August 2022}}). This started a battle between the two Spanish rivals for his rights.{{cite web |title=Barcelona did not renounce Di Stefano... they were robbed |url=https://www.sport.es/en/news/laliga/barcelona-did-not-renounce-di-5097873 |website=Sport.es |date=29 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220807002545/https://www.sport.es/en/news/laliga/barcelona-did-not-renounce-di-5097873 |archive-date=7 August 2022 |url-status=live}} FIFA appointed Armando Muñoz Calero, former president of the Spanish Football Federation, as mediator. Calero decided to let Di Stéfano play the 1953–54 and 1955–56 seasons in Madrid, and the 1954–55 and 1956–57 seasons in Barcelona.{{cite news |title=Di Stéfano y la decisión salomónica de la FIFA [Di Stéfano and the Solomonic decision of FIFA] |url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/deportes/2022/05/31/di-stefano-decision-salomonica-fifa/00031654013290888894912.htm |work=La Voz de Galicia |date=31 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220807002551/https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/deportes/2022/05/31/di-stefano-decision-salomonica-fifa/00031654013290888894912.htm |archive-date=7 August 2022 |url-status=live}} The agreement was approved by the Football Association and their respective clubs. Although the Catalans agreed, the decision created discontent among various Blaugrana members and the president was forced to resign in September 1953. Barcelona sold Madrid their half-share, and Di Stéfano moved to ''Los Blancos'', signing a four-year contract. Real paid 5.5 million Spanish pesetas for the transfer, plus a 1.3 million bonus for the purchase,{{Failed verification|date=August 2022}} an annual fee to be paid to Millonarios, and a 16,000 salary for Di Stéfano with a bonus double that of his teammates, for a total of 40% of the annual revenue of the Madrid club.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28204560 |title=BBC SPORT | Football | Alfredo Di Stefano: Did General Franco halt Barcelona transfer? |publisher=BBC News |date=7 July 2014 |access-date=2 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160208154241/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/28204560 |archive-date=8 February 2016 |url-status=live}} Di Stéfano became integral in the subsequent success achieved by Real Madrid, scoring twice in his first game against Barcelona. With him, Madrid won the first five editions of the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]].{{cite news |title=Alfredo di Stéfano was one of football's greatest trailblazers |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/jul/07/alfredo-di-stefano-real-madrid |access-date=12 October 2018 |newspaper=The Guardian |date=7 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140707201733/https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/jul/07/alfredo-di-stefano-real-madrid |archive-date=7 July 2014 |url-status=live}} The 1960s saw the rivalry reach the European stage when Real Madrid and Barcelona met twice in the European Cup, with Madrid triumphing en route to their fifth consecutive title in [[1959–60 European Cup|1959–60]] and Barcelona prevailing en route to losing the final in [[1960–61 European Cup|1960–61]]. ===Final of the bottles=== On 11 July 1968, Barcelona beat Real Madrid 1–0 in the [[1968 Copa del Generalísimo Final|Copa del Generalísimo final]] at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]]. Real Madrid fans, angry about the refereeing, started throwing bottles at the referee and Barcelona players in the last minutes of the match.{{cite web |title=La final de las botellas me hizo antimadridista |language=es |access-date=31 January 2023 |website=AS |date=11 October 2005 |url=https://as.com/futbol/2005/10/11/mas_futbol/1129012030_850215.html}} Antonio Rigo, the referee of the final, was accused of favouring Barcelona. Regarding the two not awarded penalties, he said "I didn't see a penalty on [[Amancio Amaro|Amancio]], and [[Fernando Serena|Serena]] tripped. He wanted to deceive me by [[Diving (association football)|diving]] when he entered the penalty area." He also accused the Real Madrid manager of trying to bribe him with a pre-match gift. General Franco presented the trophy to Barcelona with a pitch full of bottles, hence the name.{{cite web |title=El Barça se lleva la Copa de 'la final de las botellas' |language=es |trans-title=Barça wins the 'final of the bottles' Cup |website=Sport |date=4 April 2014 |url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/copa-del-rey/barca-lleva-copa-final-las-botellas-3242035 |access-date=31 January 2023}}{{cite web |title=1968. The "Bottle Final": Barça wins the Spanish Cup at the Bernabéu amidst a tense atmosphere |publisher=FC Barcelona |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/history/detail/card/1968-the-bottle-final-barca-wins-the-spanish-cup-at-the-bernabeu-amidst-a-tense-atmosphere |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160326220759/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/history/detail/card/1968-the-bottle-final-barca-wins-the-spanish-cup-at-the-bernabeu-amidst-a-tense-atmosphere |archive-date=26 March 2016 |df=dmy}} ===Luís Figo transfer=== [[File:Luis Figo-2009 cropped.jpg|thumb|upright|left|[[Luís Figo]]'s transfer from Barcelona to Real Madrid in 2000 resulted in a hate campaign by some of his former club's fans.]] In 2000, Real Madrid's then-presidential candidate, [[Florentino Pérez]], offered Barcelona's vice-captain [[Luís Figo]] $2.4 million to sign an agreement binding him to Madrid if he won the elections. If Figo broke the deal, he would have to pay Pérez $30 million in compensation. When his agent confirmed the deal, Figo denied everything, insisting, "I'll stay at Barcelona whether Pérez wins or loses." He accused the presidential candidate of "lying" and "fantasizing". He told Barcelona teammates [[Luis Enrique (footballer)|Luis Enrique]] and [[Pep Guardiola]] he was not leaving and they conveyed the message to the Barcelona squad.Lowe, Sid. p. 344 On 9 July, ''[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]'' ran an interview in which he said, "I want to send a message of calm to Barcelona's fans, for whom I always have and always will feel great affection. I want to assure them that Luís Figo will, with absolute certainty, be at the Camp Nou on the 24th to start the new season... I've not signed a pre-contract with a presidential candidate at Real Madrid. No. I'm not so mad as to do a thing like that." Barcelona's new president, [[Joan Gaspart]], called the media and told them, "Today, Figo gave me the impression that he wanted to do two things: get richer and stay at Barça." However, the following day, 24 July, Figo was presented in Madrid and handed his new shirt by Alfredo Di Stéfano. His buyout clause was set at $180 million. Gaspart later admitted, "Figo's move destroyed us.""[https://books.google.com/books?id=2l6zHv_reuUC&pg=PA345 Sid Lowe: Fear and loathing in La Liga.. Barcelona vs Real Madrid]" p. 345, 346. Random House. 26 September 2013 On his return to Barcelona in a Real Madrid shirt, banners with "Judas", "Scum" and "Mercenary" were hung around the stadium. Thousands of fake 10,000 peseta notes had been printed and emblazoned with his image, were among the missiles of oranges, bottles, cigarette lighters, even a couple of mobile phones were thrown at him.Lowe, Sid. p. 339 In his third season with Real Madrid, the 2002 Clásico at Camp Nou produced one of the defining images of the rivalry. Figo was taunted throughout; missiles of coins, a knife, a whisky bottle, were raining down from the stands, mostly from areas populated by the [[Boixos Nois]] where he had been taking a corner. Among the debris was a pig's head.Lowe, Sid. p. 338{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/international/3038589/Barcelona-are-braced-for-a-stiff-penalty.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/international/3038589/Barcelona-are-braced-for-a-stiff-penalty.html |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |work=The Daily Telegraph |title=Barcelona are braced for a stiff penalty |date=27 November 2002 |location=London |first=Tony |last=Jefferies}}{{cbignore}} ===Recent issues=== [[File:Pasillo Real Madrid - F.C. Barcelona.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Barcelona players performing the ''pasillo'' at the Santiago Bernabéu in 2008]] During the last decades, the rivalry has been augmented by the modern Spanish tradition of the ''pasillo'', where one team is given the guard of honor by the other team, once the former clinches the La Liga trophy before El Clásico takes place. This has happened on three occasions. First, during El Clásico that took place on 30 April 1988, in which Real Madrid had won the league championship in the previous round; then three years later, when Barcelona won the championship two rounds before El Clásico on 8 June 1991;{{cite web |author=Deportes |url=http://www.20minutos.es/noticia/376322/0/clasico/pasillo/historia/www.20minutos.es |title=(Spanish) |publisher=20minutos.es |access-date=20 October 2013}} and most recently on 7 May 2008, when Real Madrid had won the championship.{{cite web |url=http://www.futfanatico.com/2011/12/05/real-madrid-v-barcelona-glance-pasillos/ |title=Real Madrid v. Barcelona: A Glance Back at Past Pasillos | Futfanatico: Breaking Soccer News |publisher=Futfanatico |date=5 December 2011 |access-date=20 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131201014310/http://www.futfanatico.com/2011/12/05/real-madrid-v-barcelona-glance-pasillos/ |archive-date=1 December 2013 |url-status=dead}} In May 2018, Real Madrid refused to perform the ''pasillo'' for Barcelona even though the latter had already wrapped up the championship a round prior to their meeting.{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/the-pasillo-controversy-real-madrid-should-respect-barcelona/1cpzh72alhyd41pywty4c4t5ib |title=The pasillo controversy: Real Madrid should respect Barcelona with guard of honour |website=Goal.com |date=4 May 2018 |access-date=22 September 2018}} Real Madrid's coach at the time, [[Zinedine Zidane]], reasoned that Barcelona also refused to perform it five months earlier, on 23 December 2017, when Real Madrid were the [[2017 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]] champions.{{cite web |url=https://as.com/futbol/2018/05/05/primera/1525513890_587190.html |title="No le haremos pasillo al Barça porque ellos no nos lo hicieron" |website=As.com |date=5 May 2018 |language=es |access-date=26 July 2022}} The two teams met again in the [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League knockout stage#Semi-finals|semi-finals]] in 2002, with Real winning 2–0 in Barcelona and drawing 1–1 in Madrid, resulting in a 3–1 aggregate win for ''Los Blancos''. The tie was dubbed by Spanish media as the "Match of the Century".{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/7773773.stm |title=Real win Champions League showdown |work=BBC News |date=11 December 2008 |access-date=7 August 2010}} While El Clásico is regarded as one of the fiercest rivalries in world football, there have been rare moments when fans have shown praise for a player on the opposing team. In 1980, [[Laurie Cunningham]] was the first Real Madrid player to receive applause from Barcelona fans at Camp Nou; after excelling during the match, and with Madrid winning 2–0, Cunningham left the field to a standing ovation from the locals."[https://web.archive.org/web/20150324234940/http://m.fifa.com/newscentre/news/newsid=2278831/index.html Applauding the enemy]", [[FIFA|FIFA.com]], 15 February 2014"[https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/real-madrid-v-barcelona-el-clasico-preview-6290929.html Real Madrid vs Barcelona: El-Clasico Preview]", ''[[The Independent]]'', 17 January 2012, On 26 June 1983, during the second leg of the [[Copa de la Liga]] final at the Santiago Bernabéu in Madrid, having dribbled past the Real Madrid goalkeeper, Barcelona star [[Diego Maradona]] ran towards an empty goal before stopping just as the Madrid defender [[Juan José (footballer, born 1957)|Juan José]] came sliding in an attempt to block the shot and crashed into the post, before Maradona slotted the ball into the net. The manner of Maradona's goal led to many Madrid fans inside the stadium start applauding.[https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/30-years-since-maradona-stunned-the-santiago-bernabeu "30 years since Maradona stunned the Santiago Bernabéu"]. FC Barcelona. Retrieved 2 October 2014 In November 2005, [[Ronaldinho]] became the second Barcelona player to receive a standing ovation from Madrid fans at the Santiago Bernabéu. After dribbling through the Madrid defence twice to score two goals in a 3–0 win, Madrid fans paid homage to his performance with applause.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/7773778.stm |title=Rampant Ronaldinho receives standing ovation |work=BBC News |date=11 December 2008 |access-date=27 August 2010}}[https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/real-madrid-0-barcelona-3-bernabeu-forced-to-pay-homage-as-ronaldinho-soars-above-the-galacticos-516202.html "Real Madrid 0 Barcelona 3: Bernabeu forced to pay homage as Ronaldinho soars above the galacticos"]. The Independent. Retrieved 29 November 2013. On 21 November 2015, [[Andrés Iniesta]] became the third Barcelona player to receive applause from Real Madrid fans while he was substituted during a 4–0 away win, with Iniesta scoring Barça's third. He was already a popular figure throughout Spain for scoring the nation's World Cup-winning goal in 2010.{{Cite web |url=https://nesn.com/2015/11/real-madrid-fans-applaud-barcelonas-andres-iniesta-in-el-clasico-video/ |title=Real Madrid Fans Applaud Barcelona's Andres Iniesta In 'El Clasico' |publisher=NESN |date=21 November 2015 |access-date=22 November 2015}} [[File:Ronaldinho 11feb2007.jpg|thumb|right|In 2005, [[Ronaldinho]] became the second Barcelona player, after [[Diego Maradona]] in 1983, to receive a standing ovation from Real Madrid fans at the Santiago Bernabéu.]] A 2007 survey by the [[Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas]] showed that 32% of the Spanish population supported Real Madrid while 25% supported Barcelona. In third place came [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], with 5%.{{cite web |url=http://www.cis.es/cis/export/sites/default/-Archivos/Marginales/2700_2719/2705/Es2705mar_A.pdf |title=CIS Mayo 2007 |language=es |publisher=Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas |date=May 2007 |access-date=2 September 2010}} According to an Ikerfel poll in 2011, Barcelona is the most popular team in Spain with 44% of preferences, while Real Madrid is second with 37%. [[Atlético Madrid]], Valencia and [[Athletic Bilbao]] complete the top five.{{cite web |url=http://www.as.com/futbol/articulo/espana-pasa-madrid-barcelona/20111010dasdaiftb_3/Tes |title=España se pasa del Madrid al Barcelona |language=es |website=as.com |date=10 October 2011 |access-date=23 July 2012}} The rivalry intensified in 2011, when Barcelona and Real Madrid were scheduled to meet each other four times in 18 days, including the [[2011 Copa del Rey Final|Copa Del Rey final]] and [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Semi-finals|semi-finals]].{{Cite web |last=Hurtado |first=José Luis |last2=Kostopoulos |first2=Panos |date=16 April 2021|title=The 18 most intense days in the history of El Clasico |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/04/16/6079b0a9e2704e95738b45a7.html |access-date=12 May 2025|website=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]}} Several accusations of unsportsmanlike behaviour from both teams and a war of words erupted throughout the fixtures, which included four red cards. [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]] coach [[Vicente del Bosque]] stated that he was "concerned" that due to the rising hatred between the two clubs, that this could cause friction in the Spain team.{{cite web |author=Sapa-DPA |url=http://www.supersport.com/football/article.aspx?Id=415524 |title=Del Bosque concerned over Real-Barca conflict - SuperSport - Football |publisher=SuperSport |date=29 April 2011 |access-date=20 October 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107200945/http://www.supersport.com/football/article.aspx?Id=415524 |archive-date=7 November 2012}} A fixture known for its intensity and indiscipline, it has also featured [[Goal celebration|memorable goal celebrations]] from both teams, often involving mocking the opposition. In October 1999, Real Madrid forward [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]] silenced 100,000 Barcelona fans at the Camp Nou when he scored an 86th–minute equalizer before he celebrated by putting a finger to his lips as if telling the crowd to be quiet.{{cite news |title=Real Madrid-Barcelona: Celebrations in enemy territory |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/2017/04/24/58fe5ed8ca47413f548b461c.html |access-date=9 October 2018 |work=Marca}}{{cite news |title=When Raul ended Madrid's humiliation, silenced Nou Camp |url=http://www.egypttoday.com/Article/8/39224/When-Raul-ended-Madrid's-humiliation-silenced-Nou-Camp |access-date=9 October 2018 |work=Egypt Today}} In May 2009, Barcelona captain [[Carles Puyol]] kissed his Catalan armband in front of Madrid fans at the Santiago Bernabéu after his 21st–minute headed goal in a 6–2 win. [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] twice gestured to the hostile crowd to "calm down" after scoring against Barcelona at the Camp Nou in 2012 and 2016, both being the winning goals in 2–1 wins. In April 2017, in Barcelona's 3–2 win, [[Lionel Messi]] celebrated his 93rd-minute winner against Real Madrid at the Santiago Bernabéu by taking off his Barcelona shirt and holding it up to incensed Real Madrid fans – with his name and number facing them. Later that year, in August, Cristiano Ronaldo was subbed on during the 3–1 first-leg victory in the [[2017 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]], scored in the 80th minute, and took his shirt off before holding it up to Barça's fans with his name and number facing them. However, he was sent off moments later, having been awarded a second yellow card for simulation.{{cite news |title=Cristiano Ronaldo scores and is sent off in win over Barcelona |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/aug/13/barcelona-real-madrid-spanish-super-cup-match-report |work=The Guardian}} ==Player rivalries== ===László Kubala and Alfredo Di Stéfano (1953–1961)=== {{Multiple image | perrow = | total_width = 300 | align = right | image1 = Kubala.jpg | alt1 = László Kubala in 1953 | image2 = Di Stefano 1959.jpg | alt2 = Alfredo Di Stéfano | footer = [[László Kubala]] (left) and [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]] }} Until the early 1950s, Real Madrid was not a regular title contender in Spain, having won only two Primera División titles between 1929 and 1953.{{cite web |title=Primera División – Champions |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co97/records-winners-list/ |website=worldfootball.net |access-date=3 July 2022 |language=en}} However, things changed for Real after the arrival of [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]] in 1953, [[Paco Gento]] in the same year, [[Raymond Kopa]] in 1956, and [[Ferenc Puskás]] in 1958. Real Madrid's strength increased in this period until the team dominated Spain and Europe, while Barcelona relied on its Hungarian star [[László Kubala]] and [[Luis Suárez (Spanish footballer)|Luis Suárez]], who joined in 1955 in addition to the Hungarian players [[Sándor Kocsis]] and [[Zoltán Czibor]] and the Brazilian [[Evaristo (footballer)|Evaristo]]. With the arrival of Kubala and Di Stéfano, Barcelona and Real Madrid became among the most important European clubs in those years, and the players represented the turning point in the history of their teams.{{cite web |url=https://www.martiperarnau.com/el-ano-en-que-kubala-entreno-a-di-stefano/ |title=Historias de la Liga: el año en que Kubala entrenó a Di Stéfano |website=martiperarnau.com |language=es}}{{cite web |url=https://www.academia.edu/9073734 |title=Kubala e Di Stefano: le nuove stelle del cinema spagnolo durante il franchismo |website=academia.edu |language=it |last1=Sanjurjo |first1=Juan Antonio Simón}}{{cite web |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/deportes/barsa-madrid/20120420/54284642303/messi-cristiano-di-stefano-kubala-barsa-madrid.html |title=Messi y Cristiano; Di Stéfano y Kubala: La lucha entre Barça y Madrid |website=lavanguardia.com |date=19 April 2012 |language=es}} With Kubala and Di Stéfano, a rivalry was born, but it would still take a long time to become what it is today.{{cite web |url=https://spainsnews.com/real-madrid-kubalas-last-battle-against-real-madrid/ |title=Real Madrid: Kubala's last battle against Real Madrid |website=spainsnews.com |access-date=3 July 2022 |archive-date=4 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220704082114/https://spainsnews.com/real-madrid-kubalas-last-battle-against-real-madrid/ |url-status=dead}} This period was characterized by the abundance of matches in different tournaments, as they faced each other in all the tournaments available at the time, especially at the European level, where they met twice in two consecutive seasons. In their period, El Clásico was played 26 times: Real won 13 matches, Barcelona 10 matches, and 3 ended in a draw. Di Stéfano scored 14 and Kubala scored 4 goals in those matches. ===Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi (2009–2018)=== {{Main|Messi–Ronaldo rivalry}} The rivalry between [[Lionel Messi]] and [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] between 2009 and 2018 has been the most competitive in El Clásico history, with both players being their clubs' all-time top scorers. In their period, many records were broken for both clubs; the two players alternated as top scorers in La Liga and the Champions League during most seasons while they were with Real Madrid and Barcelona.{{cite web |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/cristiano-ronaldo-lionel-messi-rivalry-26494935 |title=EXCLUSIVE: Cristiano Ronaldo's former coach explains impact of Lionel Messi rivalrys |work=[[Daily Mirror]] |date=21 March 2022}} During this period, Ronaldo won the [[European Golden Shoe]] three times and Messi five times.{{cite web |title=Golden Boot ("Soulier d'Or") Awards |url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/gboot.html |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=23 January 2023}} In addition, Messi won the [[Ballon d'Or]] five times and Ronaldo four times.{{cite web |last1=White |first1=Mark |title=Every Ballon d'Or winner: A complete list of every men's player to have won the award |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/ballon-dor-complete-list-of-winners |website=FourFourTwo |access-date=23 January 2023 |language=en |date=17 October 2022}} {{Multiple image | perrow = | total_width = 300 | image1 = Lionel Messi Player of the Year 3, 2011.jpg | alt1 = Lionel Messi in 2011 | image2 = Cristiano Ronaldo609.jpg | alt2 = Cristiano Ronaldo in 2012 | footer = [[Lionel Messi]] (left) and [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] during the 2011–12 season }} During the nine years they played together in Spain, the two players scored a total of 922 goals, including 38 goals in El Clásico matches, 20 scored by Messi and 18 by Ronaldo. As of 2024, Ronaldo is [[List of UEFA Champions League top scorers|the all-time top scorer in the UEFA Champions League]], followed by Messi in the second place.{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0257-0e910cf2494a-5185150de9d4-1000--champions-league-all-time-top-scorers-cristiano-ronaldo-lionel-/ |title=Champions League all-time top scorers: Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi, Robert Lewandowski, Karim Benzema |work=[[UEFA]] |date=28 June 2022}} In addition, Messi is [[List of La Liga top scorers|the all-time top scorer of La Liga]] with 474 goals, and Ronaldo is ranked second with 311 goals.{{cite web |title=All-time La Liga top scorers: From Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo to Raul |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/lionel-messi-cristiano-ronaldo-top-10-la-liga-goalscorers-of-all-time/xrsq7xenmn81mtodnebf9q7s |website=goal.com |access-date=23 January 2023}} Both players contributed to their club's record for [[La Liga records and statistics#Most points in a La Liga season (at least 90 points)|the most points in La Liga history]], with 100 points in the [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12]] season for Real Madrid and in the [[2012–13 La Liga|2012–13]] season for Barcelona. The Messi–Ronaldo rivalry was characterized by a lot of goals scored by both players, contributing to many domestic and European titles for both teams. Their clubs were dominant in Europe, as they won six Champions League titles in nine seasons, including five consecutive seasons between 2014 and 2018.{{cite web |title=Champions League – Champions |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co19/records-winners-list/ |website=worldfootball.net |access-date=3 July 2022 |language=en}} In El Clásico matches, Messi has scored 26 goals in his career, which is the record. Ronaldo has scored 18, which is the joint second-most in the fixture's history alongside Di Stéfano. Ronaldo, on the other hand, has a slight advantage in terms of minutes per goal ratio, scoring a goal for every 141 minutes played in El Clásico matches. Only slightly behind is Messi, scoring a goal every 151.54 minutes.{{cite news |url=https://www.messivsronaldo.app/club-stats/el-clasico/ |title=Messi & Ronaldo El Clásico Stats}} In their period, the rivalry between Real Madrid and Barcelona has been encapsulated by the rivalry between Ronaldo and Messi.{{cite news |last=Bate |first=Adam |url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/12040/8974888/fear-and-loathing |title=Fear and Loathing |date=25 October 2013 |access-date=12 January 2015 |work=Sky Sports}} Following the star signings of [[Neymar]] and [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] by Barcelona, and [[Gareth Bale]] and [[Karim Benzema]] by Real Madrid, the rivalry was expanded to a battle of the clubs' attacking trios, nicknamed "BBC" (Bale–Benzema–Cristiano) and "MSN" (Messi–Suárez–Neymar).{{cite news |title=El club de los 100: MSN 91-88 BBC |url=https://www.marca.com/2015/04/17/futbol/equipos/barcelona/1429249481.html |newspaper=Marca |date=24 October 2015}} Ronaldo left Real Madrid for [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in 2018, and in the week prior to the first meeting of the teams in the [[2018–19 La Liga]], Messi sustained an arm injury, ruling him out of the match. It would be the first time since 2007 that the ''Clásico'' had featured neither player, with some in the media describing it as the 'end of an era'.{{cite web |title=Barcelona vs Real Madrid: First Clasico without Lionel Messi or Cristiano Ronaldo since 2007 marks end of era |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/first-clasico-without-lionel-messi-or-cristiano-ronaldo-since-2007-marks-end-of-an-era-for-barcelona-a3972466.html?amp |date=26 October 2018 |access-date=26 October 2018 |work=[[Evening Standard]]}}{{cite web |title=No Messi or Ronaldo in El Clasico for first time since 2007 |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/no-messi-or-ronaldo-el-clasico-first-time-2007?_format=amp |date=20 October 2018 |access-date=26 October 2018 |work=[[FourFourTwo]]}} Barcelona won the match 5–1.{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45995215 |title=Barcelona 5–1 Real Madrid |work=BBC Sport |date=28 October 2018 |access-date=28 October 2018}} ==Statistics== ===Matches summary=== {{Main|List of El Clásico matches}} {{updated|10 May 2026}} {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:85%; width: 99%; text-align: center;" |- !
